Rashi on Megillah 18a:10:1.hebrew: היסופר לו כי אדבר - הכי דריש ליה: היסופר שבחו כולו כי ארבה לו דברי שבח? אם אמר לעשות כך, כי יבולע:
Rashi on Megillah 18a:10:1.english: Shall it be told to Him when I speak - Thus he expounds it: Can all of His praise be told when I multiply words of praise for Him? If [one] says to do so, he will be swallowed up:

Rashi on Megillah 18a:11:1.hebrew: סמא דכולה משתוקא - מבחר כל הסממנין היא השתיקה, שלא להרבות דברים, והיינו "לך דומיה תהלה":
Rashi on Megillah 18a:11:1.english: The remedy of all is silence - The choicest of all remedies is silence, [that is,] not to speak excessively, and this is [the meaning of] "For You silence is praise."

Rashi on Megillah 18a:11:2.hebrew: מלה בסלע משתוקא בתרין - אם תרצה לקנות הדבור בסלע, תקנה השתיקה בשתים:
Rashi on Megillah 18a:11:2.english: A word [is worth] a sela, silence [is worth] two - If you wish to buy speech for a sela, buy silence for two.

Rashi on Megillah 18a:15:1.hebrew: קראה תרגום בכל לשון - זו ואין צ"ל זו קתני:
Rashi on Megillah 18a:15:1.english: If he read it [in] Targum, in any language - [The Mishnah] teaches [in the style of] "this, and needless to say this":

Rashi on Megillah 18a:18:1.hebrew: מיתיבי - לרב ושמואל, דקתני הכא "יוונית לא יצא":
Rashi on Megillah 18a:18:1.english: They raised an objection - against Rav and Shmuel, as it teaches here, "Greek — he has not fulfilled [his obligation]":

Rashi on Megillah 18a:18:2.english: Ivrit - the language of [the region] across the river:

Rashi on Megillah 18a:19:1.english: This is not comparable [except] - It is an answer:

Rashi on Megillah 18a:19:2.hebrew: גיפטית לגיפטים יצא - והכי נמי תנן במתני', "ללועזות בלעז":
Rashi on Megillah 18a:19:2.english: In Coptic to Copts, he has fulfilled [his obligation] - And so too we learned in the Mishnah, "[one reads it] to foreign-language speakers in a foreign language":

Rashi on Megillah 18a:1:1.hebrew: אחר ישובו בני ישראל - אחר ישובו לבית המקדש, ובקשו הקב"ה ואת דוד מלכם:
Rashi on Megillah 18a:1:1.english: Afterward the children of Israel shall return - Afterward they will return to the Temple, and seek the Holy One, blessed be He, and David their king:

Rashi on Megillah 18a:20:1.hebrew: כברייתא - זו מיתוקמא: "קראה בכל לשון" דקתני מתני' "לא יצא" — כגון גיפטית למדיים ומדית לגיפטים, אבל קורין אותו ללועזות בלעז, איש כלשונו:
Rashi on Megillah 18a:20:1.english: Like the baraita - [The Mishnah] is established like this [baraita]: [the clause] "if one read it in any [other] language" that the Mishnah teaches "he has not fulfilled [his obligation]" [refers to a case] such as Egyptian [read] to Medians, or Median [read] to Egyptians; however, they read it to foreign-language speakers in a foreign language, each person in his [own] language.

Rashi on Megillah 18a:24:1.hebrew: ופרסומי ניסא - אע"פ שאין יודעין מה ששומעין, שואלין את השומעין ואומרין: "מה היא הקרייה הזו ואיך היה הנס?" ומודיעין להן:
Rashi on Megillah 18a:24:1.english: And publicizing the miracle - Even though they do not understand what they hear, they ask those who hear [and understand] and say, "What is this reading, and how did the miracle happen?" and they inform them:

Rashi on Megillah 18a:25:1.english: The Sages did not know - [this refers to] the disciples of Rabbeinu HaKadosh [Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi]:

Rashi on Megillah 18a:26:1.hebrew: חלוגלוגות - מין ירק הוא, ושנוי בכמה מקומות במשנה ובבריית':
Rashi on Megillah 18a:26:1.english: Ḥalogelogot - It is a type of vegetable, and it is taught in several places in the Mishnah and in the Baraita.

Rashi on Megillah 18a:27:1.english: Twirling your hair - [From this] we learned that silsul is an expression of searching and turning over:

Rashi on Megillah 18a:29:1.english: Tateita - escope in Old French [meaning a broom]:

Rashi on Megillah 18a:2:1.english: Whoever sacrifices a thanks-offering - After sacrificing, give thanks:

Rashi on Megillah 18a:3:1.english: And he came down from sacrificing the sin-offering and the burnt-offering, etc.:

Rashi on Megillah 18a:6:1.english: [They] are one matter - thanksgiving too is a service of the Omnipresent:

Rashi on Megillah 18a:9:1.english: It is prohibited to declare - [His praises] by establishing a blessing:

Rashi on Megillah 18a:9:2.hebrew: למי שיכול - ואין מי שיכול לספר את כולו, לפיכך אין נראה לספר מדעתו אלא את מה שתקנו חכמים:
Rashi on Megillah 18a:9:2.english: For one who is able - And there is no one who is able to recount all of it [God's praise]; therefore, it is not fitting to recount [praises] on one's own initiative, except for what the Sages instituted:

Tosafot on Megillah 18a:17:1.hebrew: דאי סלקא דעתך למזבח קרי ליה יעקב אל - נראה דהכי נמי כתיב (שמות י״ז:ט״ו) "ויקרא שמו ה' נסי", "ויקרא לו ה' שלום" (שופטים ו׳:כ״ד), ומתרגמי' "ופלח וצלי"; מ"מ יש לומר דהתם על שם הנס ועל שם השלום שאירע להן היו קוראין למזבח כן, אבל הכא ליכא שום מעשה שנוכל לומר שע"י כן קראו יעקב "אל", ואם איתא שיעקב קראו "אל", הוי ליה לפרושי להדיא:
Tosafot on Megillah 18a:17:1.english: For if it enters your mind that Jacob called the altar El - It seems [one could object:] for so too is it written (Exodus 17:15), "And he called its name Hashem Nissi [The Lord is my miracle]," [and] "And he called it Hashem Shalom [The Lord is peace]" (Judges 6:24), and we translate [them in Targum as] "and he worshipped" and "and he prayed." Nevertheless, one can say that there, on account of the miracle and on account of the peace that occurred to them, they called the altar thus; but here, there is no event through which we could say that Jacob called it "El," and if it were so that Jacob called it "El," [the verse] should have stated [it] explicitly:
